Yes. Continue No. STOP You can’t take the credit. Check the box on line 27c." The project asks eic.us_home, "Was your main home in the United States (the 50 states and the District of Columbia) for more than half of 2025? If you were on extended active military duty outside the United States, that time counts as a main home in the United States" (forms/2025/eic.yaml; the interview prompt is the same), with no spouse clause, and reads it on joint returns too. The model is right: a joint filer without a qualifying child whose own main home was in the United States and whose spouse’s was not passes Step 4 and is allowed the credit. The rest of the restatement (the eic.credit helper, Worksheets A and B) matches, as the model says. Witness: stage9.eic.joint.no_child.12000 (joint, no qualifying child, $12,000.00 wages, eic.us_home yes): project line 27a $649.00, line 27c unchecked (evaluated). If the spouse’s main home was outside the United States for more than half of 2025, the source gives $0.00 and the box checked; the filer’s own home was in the United States, so the project’s question is truthfully answered yes and the $649.00 stays. rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.separated_spouses_box (owner's decision, 2026-10-26). The model compares the restatement with the printed box wording, which has no EIC conditions. The only instructions for the box are the earned income credit's: i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 6, "No. Check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses on page 1 of Form 1040 or 1040-SR", and p. 44, Special rule for separated spouses, "If you meet these requirements, make sure you check the box in the Dependents section". The register records both readings (checked only under the EIC special rule, or whenever the printed condition holds) and the first is chosen; the rendered English states the chosen reading (eic.separated_box) accurately.
